questions.prompt: Where does Anthropic say automated evals are especially useful?

options.text: Pre-launch and in CI/CD, on each change and model upgrade
options.explanation: Right. They are the first line of defense against quality problems.

options.text: Only after launch, in place of production monitoring
options.explanation: Anthropic pairs automated evals with production monitoring, which covers post-launch drift.

options.text: Once a year, as a final check before a big release
options.explanation: The post says to run them on each agent change, not rarely.

questions.prompt: What do the Claude Code docs say about secrets on fork pull requests in public repos?

options.text: GitHub passes the secrets to every fork run automatically
options.explanation: The docs say the opposite for public repositories.

options.text: GitHub withholds secrets from fork pull request runs
options.explanation: Right. So an eval that needs an API key will not run for those pull requests.

options.text: Forks get a read-only copy of the maintainers' API key
options.explanation: The docs do not describe this. Secrets are withheld.

questions.prompt: Why keep tasks and graders as files in your own repo?

options.text: CI systems can only run files and never call a vendor API
options.explanation: CI can call APIs. This is not the reason.

options.text: Vendor dashboards cannot run evals with more than one trial
options.explanation: The lesson's reason is control: vendor tools can change or close.

options.text: Vendor tools can change or close; files let you switch runner
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's Evals platform is scheduled to shut down on November 30, 2026.
